Week 5 — Defend one number

Pick one hospital and one measure. By the end you will have a one-page defense of that single number: what kind of number it is, what it was counted from, when, what was hidden, how it compares, and what it does not tell you. The notebook gathers the facts from the file. AI can help you draft the page; the ideas and decisions must be yours. Make sure every claim is one you can explain live, in class, without the AI open — that explanation is what verifies the work.

Write your defense

Fill in the three boxes. The page below combines your answers with the facts from the file. AI can help you draft and tighten it; before you submit, read every sentence and ask "could I explain this live, without the AI open?" A defense you can't say out loud isn't a defense.

Defense of one number — DRAFT

BRIDGEPORT HOSPITAL (070010, CT) · READM_30_HF · value 21.7 What it means. (write this yourself) What kind of number. a rate ("Heart failure (HF) 30-Day Readmission Rate"). The file does not state the unit; the median across hospitals is 21.3. Confirm the unit in the measure definition. Counted from. Denominator (as labeled in the file): 1400; Number of Patients Returned: Not Applicable — for this measure 0 of 4,790 rows hold a number, so the file does not give you a numerator. Say so. When. 07/01/2023 to 06/30/2025. This file mixes 5 different reporting period(s) across its measures — check that anything you compare it with covers the same months. What is hidden. Footnote on this row: (none). For this measure, 1,537 of 4,790 hospitals have no number. Footnote codes seen: (none) (3,194), 1 (1,020), 5 (338), 19 (172), 29 (58), 7 (7). Footnote numbers are codes: look up what each means in CMS's footnote list for this dataset (linked from the source page). Do not guess. Compared with. "Compared to National" is Not Available for every hospital on this measure in this release (4,790 rows). You cannot cite a CMS comparison; you can only say where it sits: higher than 61% of the 3,253 hospitals with a number for this measure (median 21.3). Why I believe it. (write this yourself) What I won't claim. (write this yourself) Draft assembled by the notebook from the source file. Every claim is one I can explain without the AI open.

Ask your AI — draft, then stress-test AI can help you draft this; make sure every claim is one you can explain live, without the AI open. Once you have a draft, paste it and:
"Here is my one-page defense of a CMS hospital measure. List every claim in it, and for each one tell me whether it is supported by the facts I gave, needs a source I haven't cited (for example the measure definition or the CMS footnote list), or is wrong. Ask me two questions a skeptical hospital executive would ask."
Then make sure you can answer the two questions yourself, out loud — that is what show and explain is for.

Before you submit

Deliverable: a one-page defense of one number — what it is, numerator and denominator (or why the file doesn't give them), suppression and footnotes, reporting period, how it compares, and what it does not tell you. AI may help draft it; every claim must be one you can explain live without the AI open. Submit your AI transcript with it. The one check to run: open the measure definition on the CMS source page and confirm the unit and the patient population you describe. If you can't find it, write "not confirmed" rather than guess. Sign-off (write three lines in your submission):
  • What I checked myself: …
  • What I'm trusting the AI on: …
  • What I won't sign: …
